verdict: This reference is usable but should not be treated as settled, and the honest parts of it make the unflagged parts more dangerous rather than less: the adjudicator demonstrably understood the transcribe-do-not-edit rule, keeping `o njegove epistemologiji`, `prema državi kao organizaciju`, `daju određene poslove` and `to je uopšte nije zakonska kategorija` in their ungrammatical spoken form, and flagged seventeen spans on uvod-u-pravo alone. That makes the four places where it silently supplied better Serbian than any engine produced look like lapses in an otherwise applied rule rather than a policy, and a reviewer will not find them by reading the flag list. The weakest clip is by far uvod-u-pravo, whose audio is poor enough that large stretches of the reference are reconstruction: `funkcionisanja države` at 00:08, `službenom licu` at 01:58 and `državnih organa` at 02:25 each replace a form that no engine produced with the word the legal context predicts, and each has a flagged twin elsewhere in the clip, so the flagging was inconsistent rather than absent. `Subordinacija je odnos` at 00:15 overrides a two-engine majority to produce a grammatical copula. Because three of these four corrections are exactly what an LLM correction pass would also do, the `--fix` axis on uvod-u-pravo is measuring partly against its own output and its margin there should be discounted until a human confirms those four spans. gozba-sample is in much better shape, with clean audio, high engine agreement, and only one real omission: groq was recorded as silent in window 6 when it had in fact emitted that clause early and two tokens shorter. The single highest-leverage action for a reviewer is not any individual span but the `Locke`/`Lok`/`Džon Lok` orthography decision the adjudicator already raised, since it moves WER on every occurrence in the clip and no amount of adjudication can settle a spelling convention.
